description: Shared Renovate posture for every nanohype repo. Consume it with a one-line renovate.json: {"extends": ["github>nanohype/.github"]}.

This exists because the posture was previously copy-pasted into six repos and had already drifted: five carried automerge rules and eks-gitops carried none, and one copy needed a config migration the others did not. A tooling preset belongs in one consumed place, not in per-repo copies.

MATCHER HAZARD, read before writing a packageRule for the security path: there isn't one. isVulnerabilityAlert is NOT a packageRules matcher, so a rule carrying it is narrowed only by its match* fields — one written as matchUpdateTypes patch/minor/major matches every update in the repo. This preset held exactly that rule, and the cost was invisible from inside it: it stamped 'security' on all 75 open dependency PRs across the org, so a real CVE fix looked identical to a typescript major, and its labels array replaced the 'major' label the rule above sets, so no major upgrade was flagged as one anywhere. Both failures are the same shape — a signal that fires on everything carries nothing. The security posture belongs in the vulnerabilityAlerts block, which is the supported mechanism, and automerge is already false on the patch/minor and major rules independently, so nothing is holding it shut from here.

ORDERING HAZARD, read before adding a repo-local packageRule: a consumer's packageRules are appended AFTER the ones here, and later rules win. Settings in this preset are defeatable that way. A local rule setting automerge:true would land after the patch/minor and major rules that set it false and would win — and unlike the rules here it would apply to CVE-driven updates too, since vulnerabilityAlerts cannot re-disable what a packageRule turned on. A local rule setting minimumReleaseAge would likewise override the first-party exemptions at the end of this array: on @shuttering, a floor Renovate holds that pnpm does not is a bump that never gets proposed, and on nanohype/.github, the floor holds the whole github-actions group branch pending. Local rules also apply after the lockFileMaintenance block, so one matching lock file maintenance that sets minimumReleaseAge or minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour replaces what that block sets.

TITLE CONTRACT: 'deps' is the semantic SCOPE, never the semantic TYPE. Renovate's PR title is the first thing a conventional-commit gate reads, and a type outside that gate's allowed list makes every PR this preset opens unmergeable in that repo — with no signal anywhere else, because a repo without such a gate merges the same title happily. Keep the type inside the conventional set (chore); express what is being updated in the scope.

AGE FLOOR: minimumReleaseAge holds routine updates for three days. Partly that is supply-chain posture — a compromised publish is typically caught and unpublished within hours, and no dependency here is urgent enough to be worth being the first consumer of. Mostly it is so this preset stops proposing work the package managers will refuse. pnpm 11 defaults minimumReleaseAge to 1440 minutes AND re-verifies every entry in the lockfile on every install, not just the ones being added, so a single too-young package anywhere in the tree fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in repos that never touched it. Renovate's floor has to stay at or above the package manager's, or Renovate writes lockfiles that its own CI rejects. Three days leaves headroom over pnpm's one, and costs nothing against the weekly schedule already in force.

GO.SUM: postUpdateOptions runs `go mod tidy` after every gomod update. Without it Renovate rewrites go.mod and adds the new checksums to go.sum but leaves the replaced versions' lines behind, so a repo whose CI checks that go.mod and go.sum are tidy rejects every Go update this preset opens, and the PR needs a hand-pushed tidy commit before it can merge.

The security path opts out on purpose: vulnerabilityAlerts sets minimumReleaseAge to null so a CVE fix is proposed the moment it exists. When the fix itself is hours old that can still produce a PR pnpm declines to install until it ages out. Opening it immediately is the point — the PR is the signal a human needs — and it goes green on a re-run without any config change.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Lock file maintenance keeps the top-level floor and sets minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to timestamp-optional. Its update regenerates a lockfile rather than moving a dependency to a release, so it carries no release timestamp, and under timestamp-required, Renovate's default, an update with a floor and no timestamp keeps renovate/stability-days pending and the branch never passes. timestamp-optional lets an update with no timestamp pass that check, and set in this block it reaches lock file maintenance alone: every other update under a floor still needs a timestamp old enough to pass. The floor stays because Renovate hands it to the tools that take one during regeneration. npm resolves with --before at the floor, or by its own min-release-age when the consumer's .npmrc sets one, and Poetry runs with POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE, which Poetry 2.4.0 and later honor. pnpm takes nothing from Renovate and applies its own minimumReleaseAge, which pnpm 11 defaults to 1440 minutes. Nothing else gets a floor from Renovate on this branch: Renovate refreshes .terraform.lock.hcl itself, to the newest provider version each lock's constraints allow, and yarn, Cargo, Helm and the rest are floored only by whatever their own configuration sets. A null minimumReleaseAge here would unblock the branch as well, and would take --before away from every npm consumer whose .npmrc sets no min-release-age.

packageRules.description: Patch + minor open a PR and wait for a human. automergeType is 'pr' rather than 'branch' for whenever automerge is switched on: 'branch' commits straight to the base branch without ever opening a PR, which this org does not do.
Group AWS SDK v2 (go) — they release together
Group @aws-sdk/* with @smithy/* (npm) — the SDK and the runtime it is generated against release together, and splitting them produces PRs that cannot pass CI alone.
Group k8s.io/* — they must move together
Group @opentelemetry/* — the SDK, exporters and instrumentations move together
Group the Postgres client with its types

Group the whole eslint stack — @eslint/* core packages, typescript-eslint, plugins and shared configs. A flat-config eslint upgrade that moves @eslint/js without its plugins fails lint on its own, so they travel together.
GitHub Actions — group minor + patch into one PR
Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs (supply-chain hardening)

First-party packages skip the release-age floor. The floor exists so no tree here is the first consumer of a compromised publish — a hijacked package is usually caught and unpublished within hours. @shuttering is published from a repo under the same ownership as its consumers, deliberately and announced, so there is no third party to be compromised by and the floor only delays a bump by three days. This has to match the pnpm side: consuming repos carry minimumReleaseAgeExclude for the same scope, and if Renovate kept the floor while pnpm dropped it, Renovate would simply refuse to propose an upgrade the package manager was willing to install. Deliberately NOT extended to @nanohype/*, which is published to the public registry and consumed outside this org — it is held to the same bar as any other public dependency.

First-party action refs skip the release-age floor. A ref to a branch of a repository this org owns, such as nanohype/.github/actions/merge-gate@<sha> # main, has no release to age, and no third party to be compromised by. Renovate raises a digest update for that pin whenever the branch moves, and the update reaches the branch status check with no release timestamp, so under minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required the floor keeps renovate/stability-days pending for as long as the branch exists, and the github-actions group branch the update lands in is held with it. Unlike the @shuttering exemption this one has no install-time half, since pnpm install never reads an action ref. pnpm outdated and pnpm update read action refs only when --include-github-actions or update.githubActions opts in, and hold them to minimumReleaseAge in pnpm 11 from 11.28.0 and in pnpm 12 from 12.7.0, matching minimumReleaseAgeExclude against the action and repository names, so a consumer that updates actions that way lists nanohype/.github there for the same exemption. The name is exact rather than a pattern, so a lookalike such as nanohype/.github-evil or evil/.github keeps the floor, and matchManagers keeps the exemption to the github-actions manager. It is matched on depName as well as packageName because a ref with an explicit host, such as https://gitea.example.com/nanohype/.github/actions/x@<sha>, has the packageName nanohype/.github on a server this org does not own; only a ref with no host has the depName nanohype/.github, so a first-party ref is written without one, and a ref that spells out https://github.com/ keeps the floor. Renovate matches names as case-insensitive globs and as regexes, so a later rule that sets minimumReleaseAge and can match this ref, through '*', a glob, a regex, a negation or a different case, puts the floor back; a rule like that goes above this one.

customManagers.description: Track versions pinned in workflow env vars. A CI job that installs a tool by asking a release API for 'latest' has no pinned version to bump, so its behaviour changes with no commit and a gate can go red on a diff it never read. Pinning fixes that and creates the opposite problem — a version nobody updates — unless something tracks it. Annotate the line and this manager treats it as a dependency: # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=owner/repo

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The whole security posture lives here, not in packageRules — see MATCHER HAZARD in the top-level description for why a packageRule cannot express 'only vulnerability alerts'. minimumReleaseAge is null on purpose, stated rather than inherited: the top-level three-day floor must not delay a CVE fix. Renovate already defaults this block that way, and writing it down keeps a future edit to the top-level floor from silently acquiring a delay on the security path.
